name: Pascal
note: Wirth's teaching language emphasising structured programming and strong typing
typeSystem: Static, strong, with a rich set of built-in structured types (records, arrays, sets, enumerations, and pointers) designed explicitly to encourage structured programming and catch mistakes at compile time.
runtime: Historically compiled to a portable intermediate 'p-code' interpreted by a small virtual machine (the UCSD p-System), or compiled ahead-of-time straight to native code (Turbo Pascal and most modern compilers).

runtimes.name: Native (Free Pascal, Turbo Pascal)
runtimes.role: AOT compiles Pascal to native machine code.

runtimes.name: UCSD p-System
runtimes.role: Historic portable bytecode ('p-code') interpreter that let Pascal programs run unmodified across many 1970s-80s microcomputers.

compilers.name: Free Pascal
compilers.role: Modern, actively maintained open-source native compiler.

compilers.name: Turbo Pascal
compilers.role: Borland's hugely popular, extremely fast native compiler for MS-DOS and Windows.

concurrencyModel: Standard Pascal has no built-in concurrency; later dialects and libraries (e.g. Free Pascal's threading units) add OS-thread support on top.
